subject: gk
concept: Government Policies and Schemes        , Educational Policies
question: Which major reform was introduced in the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020?

options.text: Replacement of the 10+2 system with a 5 + 3 + 3 + 4 structure
Mandatory board exams for all grades

solution:
The correct answer is __**Replacement of the 10+2 system with a 5 + 3 + 3 + 4 structure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 introduced a new structural framework for school education, replacing the 10+2 system with the **5+3+3+4 structure**.
 
• The **5+3+3+4 structure** corresponds to the foundational stage (ages 3–8), preparatory stage (ages 8–11), middle stage (ages 11–14), and secondary stage (ages 14–18).
 
• This reform emphasizes the importance of **early childhood care and education (ECCE)**, integrating preschool education into the formal schooling system.
 
• The new structure aims to align the Indian education system with global standards and emphasizes **experiential, skill-based, and holistic learning**.
 
• It also focuses on reducing the rigid separations between academic streams, vocational education, and extracurricular activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Foundational Stage**: Covers ages 3–8, including three years of preschool and two years of primary education. It focuses on play-based and activity-based learning.
 
• **Preparatory Stage**: Covers ages 8–11 (grades 3–5) and emphasizes discovery-based and interactive classroom learning.
 
• **Middle Stage**: Covers ages 11–14 (grades 6–8) and introduces subject-specific learning, including vocational education.
 
• **Secondary Stage**: Covers ages 14–18 (grades 9–12) and allows students to choose subjects based on their interests, with a multidisciplinary approach.
 
• **Other Reforms under NEP 2020**: Focus on mother tongue/local language as the medium of instruction, introduction of coding and computational thinking from an early stage, and flexibility for students to select subjects across streams.
